SYNTHETIC TEST DOCUMENT - FICTIONAL PATIENT - NOT FOR CLINICAL USE
COLONOSCOPY REPORT
Facility: Pinecrest Endoscopy Center (fictional)
Patient: Harold Imbrie (fictional)
Date of service: November 3, 2026
Endoscopist: Beatrix Lowenthal, MD (fictional)
Indication: Intermittent bright red blood per rectum.
History: The last colonoscopy, in August 2021, showed small internal hemorrhoids only.
No polypectomy was performed at the last colonoscopy; none was performed today either.
Procedure: The colonoscope was advanced to the cecum and into the terminal ileum.
Bowel preparation was good.
Findings:
- Terminal ileum: normal.
- Colon: normal mucosa throughout; no polyps, masses or sites of bleeding.
- Rectum: small non-bleeding internal hemorrhoids on retroflexion.
Impression:
1. Small internal hemorrhoids, the likely source of the bleeding.
2. Otherwise normal colonoscopy to the terminal ileum.
Plan: Fiber supplementation; clinic follow-up as needed.
